title: Embedding model contract stability and rollback playbook
creator: Priya Desai
description: Create a reproducible, tenant-safe onboarding and versioning playbook for new embedding models and reranker pairs. Focus on contract stability, rollback safety, and measurable quality/latency regressions at each rollout stage. This ticket covers engineering work: gating logic in the embed gateway, migration tooling for tenant embeddings, telemetry for A/B and MRR-based quality checks, and automated rollback triggers tied to SLA breaches or quality drops.
acceptance_criteria: A stable model contract spec checked at runtime (dimensionality, vector dtype, L2/inner prod semantics) with automatic rejection of incompatible model variants
A canary gating circuit that can limit traffic by tenant and region with percent-based ramps and rapid rollback on signal
Migration tool to re-embed a tenant's corpus with a new model that runs incremental / idempotent re-embedding and exposes progress metrics
End-to-end telemetry dashboard capturing embedding latency p50/p95, vector norm drift, ANN recall@k, downstream reranker MRR/NDCG, and end-to-end p50/p95 for embed+rerank
Automated rollback policy that triggers on combined signals (latency SLA breach OR quality regression > 5% absolute in baseline metrics) and provides diagnostics artifact bundle for postmortem

technical_notes: Model contract checks: validate output vector shape, dtype (float32/float16/int8), and embedding semantics header (is_normalized boolean). Fail fast in gateway to avoid polluting ANN indices.

ANN index considerations: new embeddings may change nearest-neighbor distribution. Recommendation: create shadow index per-tenant during canary and compare recall@k against baseline before switching read path.
Reranking latency budget: target end-to-end embed+retrieve+rerank p50 < 60ms for small queries; p95 < 200ms. If reranker increases tail latency, rollout must be paused.
KV cache interactions: when switching model families, invalidate per-tenant prefix caches and add short-lived compatibility cache layer to serve mixed-model responses during migration.

Migration tool: idempotent job that reads tenant doc id list, computes new embeddings, writes to a tenant-scoped versioned vector table and triggers ANN index merge for serving. Support dry-run mode that emits sample metrics without committing.
Data retention: keep both old and new embeddings for 30 days tagged by model_version to support quick rollbacks and offline evaluation comparisons.
Fallbacks: route traffic to last-known-good model variant if new model fails contract checks or signals are abnormal. Provide an explicit metric link in the console for quick diagnosis.
rollout_plan: Stage 0 (alpha internal): deploy variant, run contract checks, create shadow index, run offline MRR/NDCG evaluation on reference prompt set. (5 internal tenants)

Stage 1 (tenant-scoped canary): enable for specific low-risk tenants at 1-5% traffic. Monitor embed_latency_ms, ann_recall_at_10, reranker_mrr_100 for 24-72h. Stop/revert on SLA breach or quality drop >5%.
Stage 2 (broad canary): expand to 10-25% traffic across regions with mixed tenant types. Run live A/B with holdout baseline and compute statistical significance for MRR/NDCG over 7 days.
Stage 3 (general availability): if no regressions and latency targets met, mark model variant as GA and switch tenant default. Schedule deprecation timeline for superseded model (30d notice).
Emergency rollback: immediate traffic cut to previous variant and surface diagnostic bundle (sample queries, embedding diffs, ANN recall reports, console link).
risks: Embedding distribution shift reducing ANN recall for retrieval-heavy tenants leading to silent quality degradation
Indexer rebuilds or shadow indices increase cost and storage temporarily
Rollback complexity for tenants that performed downstream re-ranking model finetune on new embeddings
Tail latency increase from reranker incompatibilities impacting SLOs
Edge-case: quantized int8 variants producing different similarity semantics if not normalized consistently
